frozen_candidate_root_contribution: A single delineated traversable roadway — a bounded course/thoroughfare along which one proceeds from a starting point toward a destination. The root names the physical medium-of-passage itself (the road), not the direction of travel, the quality of the road, or the goal reached; those are supplied by construction (إلى/على/عن), by attributive modifiers (مستقيم, سوي, الجحيم), and by context.

internal_discovery.candidate_root_contribution: A single delineated traversable roadway — a bounded course/thoroughfare along which one proceeds from a starting point toward a destination. The root names the physical medium-of-passage itself (the road), not the direction of travel, the quality of the road, or the goal reached; those are supplied by construction (إلى/على/عن), by attributive modifiers (مستقيم, سوي, الجحيم), and by context.
internal_discovery.plain_explanation: Every one of the 45 occurrences is the noun صِرَاط, and in each the recoverable invariant is "a road/route to be walked." The most decisive evidence is the small set of occurrences where the surrounding theology strips away and a bare, near-physical road remains: 7:86 warns highwaymen not to "sit by every road" (بِكُلِّ صِرَاطٍ) to intercept believers — this is a literal thoroughfare where travelers pass; 7:16 has Iblīs vow to "sit on your road" (صِرَاطَكَ ٱلْمُسْتَقِيمَ) to ambush; 36:66 pictures people who, blinded, would "race along the road" (فَٱسْتَبَقُوا۟ ٱلصِّرَاطَ) yet cannot see it — a road as a physically negotiated surface. These anchor the concrete core: a course one physically traverses. From this base the abstract 'way of life / religion' sense is an internally bridged extension: 6:153 explicitly places صِرَاطِى (my road, singular) in contrast with ٱلسُّبُل (the branching ways one must not follow), i.e. the same road-image used for a course of conduct. That the root supplies only the road — never the direction — is shown by 37:23, where the identical noun points toward Hell (إِلَىٰ صِرَاطِ ٱلْجَحِيمِ): the road can lead anywhere, so the destination is contributed by إلى + genitive, not by ص ر ط. Likewise the pervasive مُّسْتَقِيم ('straight') is a separate attribute (root qwm): the noun occurs bare and un-straight in 23:74 (عَنِ ٱلصِّرَاطِ لَنَاكِبُونَ — deviating off the road), 36:66, 38:22 (سَوَآءِ ٱلصِّرَاطِ — the even middle of the road), and 7:86, proving straightness is added, not intrinsic. The prepositions map cleanly onto a road-schema: إِلَىٰ صِرَٰطٍ (guidance TO / onto a road: 1:6, 2:142, 6:87, 5:16, 16:121, 24:46, 42:52, 22:24, 37:23, etc.), عَلَىٰ صِرَٰطٍ (being ON/standing upon the road: 11:56 of the Lord, 36:4, 43:43, 67:22, 6:39, 16:76), and عَنِ ٱلصِّرَٰطِ (turning OFF the road: 23:74). Even the hardest cases resolve to 'road': 15:41 (صِرَٰطٌ عَلَىَّ مُسْتَقِيمٌ) = a road that runs straight up to / is incumbent upon Me; 11:56 (رَبِّى عَلَىٰ صِرَٰطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ) = the Lord stands upon a straight road (i.e. His governance runs a straight course). In every family — literal ambush-road, guidance-destination road, standing-upon road, road-to-Hell, the even-middle-of-the-road — subtracting form (invariant: all N), construction (the preposition/case vector), participants, and context leaves exactly one thing: the traversable roadway.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: FORM: all 45 are the same noun صِرَاط (QAC 'N'); no verb/participle/passive variation exists, so morphology adds nothing beyond nominalizing 'the road' — it cannot be the source of any sense-difference. CONSTRUCTION: the directional/locative senses come entirely from prepositions and case — إِلَىٰ (onto/toward the road: destination vector), عَلَىٰ (upon/standing-on the road: location vector), عَنْ (off/away from the road: departure vector), and bare accusative object of هَدَى (guided [him onto] a road: 4:68, 48:2, 48:20, 37:118). These vectors are NOT in the root. PARTICIPANTS: subjects/objects (God guiding, the Prophet calling, Iblīs ambushing, waylayers sitting, the deviators turning off) vary freely and leave the road-meaning untouched. CONTEXT/ATTRIBUTES: 'straight/right' is مُّسْتَقِيم / سَوِيّ / سَوَآء (root qwm/swy), 'Hell' is ٱلْجَحِيم, 'the Almighty' is ٱلْعَزِيز ٱلْحَمِيد — all attributive genitives/adjectives external to ص ر ط. After removing all four layers the constant residue in all 45 is: a bounded traversable roadway.
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: The hardest occurrence is 15:41: قَالَ هَٰذَا صِرَٰطٌ عَلَىَّ مُسْتَقِيمٌ. On one reading صِرَاط here shades toward 'a binding rule/principle upon Me,' which could look like an abstract obligation rather than a road. But it reconciles cleanly without abandoning the residue: the construction عَلَىَّ مُسْتَقِيمٌ describes a road that runs straight up to / terminates at the speaker (God) — 'a road [leading] straight to Me' — parallel to the physical على-road frames in 11:56 (رَبِّى عَلَىٰ صِرَٰطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ) and 36:4. The apparent 'obligation/incumbency' nuance is contributed by the preposition عَلَىٰ + 1st-person pronoun, not by the noun; strip it and the road-image remains. So the residue is recoverable, and the seeming abstraction is a construction effect. (Runner-up hard case, 37:23 صِرَٰطِ ٱلْجَحِيمِ, is actually confirmatory: a road to Hell shows the root supplies only the road, never a positive destination.)
internal_discovery.competing_hypothesis: The strongest alternative core is 'the straight/right way (of religion/conduct)' — i.e. building rectitude or normative correctness into the root itself, since 30+ of 45 occurrences pair صِرَاط with مُّسْتَقِيم and denote the true religion. Internal evidence arbitrates decisively AGAINST folding straightness into the root: (1) the noun occurs bare and explicitly non-straight — 37:23 'road of Hell,' 23:74 people 'deviating off the road,' 38:22 'the even middle of the road' (سواء needed precisely because straightness is not given), 7:86 'every road' used by waylayers; (2) 'straight' is always a separable adjective from a different root (qwm/swy) which itself varies (مُّسْتَقِيم vs سَوِيّ vs سَوَآء). Since the root's contribution must be present in ALL 45 including the Hell-road and the ambush-roads, the invariant can only be 'roadway,' with rectitude an external modifier. The competing hypothesis over-reads the frequent collocation as if it were lexical content.
internal_discovery.distinctiveness_note: Nearest semantic neighbors are SBL (سَبِيل 'way/path/means') and TrQ (طَرِيق 'road/track'). Internal arbitration is available: 6:153 sets صِرَاطِى (my road, SINGULAR, the one to be followed) against ٱلسُّبُل (the plural branching ways that scatter you off it), and 7:86 contrasts بِكُلِّ صِرَاطٍ (every road, where waylayers sit) with صَدّ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ (barring from God's way). This suggests صِرَاط's distinctive contribution is the single, physically-negotiated main thoroughfare/highway one is ON, whereas سَبِيل leans toward the way-as-course/means (hence pluralizes freely and takes 'means' senses). صِرَاط is never pluralized in this data and is consistently the concrete surface one walks, stands on, races along, or is ambushed on. Falsifiability condition: if a confirmed occurrence showed صِرَاط pluralized, or used as an abstract 'means/instrumentality' with no traversable-road image recoverable (e.g. 'by the ṣirāṭ of wealth' meaning 'by means of'), the 'single traversable thoroughfare' residue would be falsified and would collapse toward the more diffuse SBL sense.
internal_discovery.rationale: A single non-empty contribution — 'a bounded traversable roadway/course one proceeds along' — is surface-recoverable in every one of the 45 occurrences, with a determinate concrete center anchored by the near-literal road occurrences (7:86 waylayers sitting by every road; 7:16 Iblīs sitting on the road; 36:66 racing along the road; 38:22 the even middle of the road). Because the root is morphologically monomorphic (all 45 = the noun صِرَاط), form-layer noise is nil, and the sense-variation that exists is fully attributable to external layers: prepositions/case supply direction (إلى/على/عن), and separate-root adjectives supply quality (مستقيم, سوي). The two facts that could threaten unity — the ubiquitous 'straight' pairing and the 15:41 'incumbent-upon-Me' reading — both resolve as external-layer contributions, and the Hell-road (37:23) plus the bare deviation/ambush roads positively prove the root itself is direction- and value-neutral. The abstract 'way of religion/conduct' sense is a metaphorical extension internally bridged by 6:153's own road-vs-branching-ways contrast, so no forcing is required. Distinctiveness from سبيل/طريق is internally supported (singular main thoroughfare vs plural branching ways/means) with a clear falsifiability condition. Unity holds against the hardest cases without any unreconciled occurrence, warranting PREFERRED at STRONG strength.

adversarial_verification.notes: Adversarial sweep of all 45 occurrences (all single noun form N, صِرَاط) found no genuine failing occurrence. The unity ('a single delineated traversable roadway; direction/quality/goal supplied by construction') holds across every family: (a) near-physical anchors 7:86 بِكُلِّ صِرَٰطٍ, 7:16 صِرَٰطَكَ, 36:66 ٱسْتَبَقُوا۟ ٱلصِّرَٰطَ, 23:74 عَنِ ٱلصِّرَٰطِ, 38:22 سَوَآءِ ٱلصِّرَٰطِ retain the road-as-traversed-surface core; (b) guidance-TO road (إلى+gen supplies destination) — decisively confirmed by the FALSIFIER 37:23 إِلَىٰ صِرَٰطِ ٱلْجَحِيمِ, where the identical noun points to Hell, proving the goal is NOT in the root; (c) على-locative (11:56, 36:4, 43:43, 67:22, 6:39, 16:76); (d) predicate 'this is a straight road' religion sense (3:51, 19:36, 36:61, 43:61, 43:64, 6:126, 6:153), bridged internally by the road image. Hardest cases 15:41 (صِرَٰطٌ عَلَىَّ مُسْتَقِيمٌ) and 11:56 (رَبِّى عَلَىٰ صِرَٰطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ) are metaphorical applications to God's governance/obligation, but they DECOMPOSE cleanly under the candidate's own compositional thesis (root=road, على=vector, مستقيم=quality) rather than breaking it — resolution is non-circular standard image-schema metaphor, not ad-hoc. Quality is demonstrably added, not intrinsic: bare-noun un-straight cases 7:86, 23:74, 36:66 co-exist with the pervasive مستقيم/سوي attribute (qwm/swy roots). Distinctiveness: صِرَاط is always singular/never pluralized in-corpus, imaged as one bounded main thoroughfare, explicitly contrasted with branching ٱلسُّبُل in 6:153 (صِرَٰطِى مُسْتَقِيمًا … وَلَا تَتَّبِعُوا۟ ٱلسُّبُلَ) — a genuine discriminator against nearest neighbors SBL (سبيل, pluralizes, can mean means/cause) and طريق. Range from concrete road to 'way of religion' is polysemy along a single road image, not homonymy — so no semantic split for the candidate to fail on. Falsifiable failure condition (direction/goal/quality intrinsic to root, or unbridgeable split) is not met by any occurrence.
